text: Good evening. I'd like to call the August 11th, 2026 School Board Business Meeting to order. Before we begin this meeting, I'd like to thank everyone for attending this evening and remind the audience that comments to this board may only be made at the podium during the public comment period.

Comments from the audience are prohibited and in violation of Section 18.2-415 of the Code of Virginia. Disorderly Conduct in Public Places, and School Board Policy 6141. I appreciate everyone's patience and understanding so that we can conduct the business meeting in an orderly fashion.

We will now have an invocation by Mr. Pronto, followed by the flag salute led by Dr. Darby. Before tonight's invocation, we would like to take a moment to honor and remember two students and two members of our CCPS family who have recently passed away.

Following these remembrances, we ask that you join us in observing a moment of silence in their memory. We pause to remember Aubrey Green, also known as Breezy. Although his time at Midlothian High School was brief, Breezy made meaningful connections with faculty and fellow students who will deeply miss him.

An entrepreneur at heart, Breezy had even started his own lemonade stand, reflecting his bright spirit and personality. His impact was evident in the kindness and condolences shared by classmates following his passing. We pause to remember Will Schaefer, a student who attended Midlothian High School during his ninth grade year and continued his education through CCPS Online during his 10th grade year.

Will is remembered as a quiet and kind young man whose gentle nature left an impression on those who knew him. We pause to honor the memory of a deeply valued member of our CCPS family, Mrs. Elanda Boyd, who began her dedicated career with us in 1998.

Over nearly three decades of service, Mrs. Boyd supported our schools in numerous capacities, brilliantly anchoring the vital work between our district and our custodial vendors. In her most recent role, she spent countless hours molding, mentoring, and enriching the lives of everyone she encountered.

Though she was quiet, soft-spoken, and a woman of few words, her input and influence spoke volumes. Mrs. Boyd truly exemplified the high standards required to both lead and support, taking immense pride in her team, her schools, and in being a woman of excellence.

Upon her desk, her decorative plaque still shines as a testament to her spirit. Act like a lady, think like a boss. That simple phrase perfectly reflected the strength, grace, and determination she brought to work every single day.

While we continue to mourn her passing, we are profoundly grateful for the unsung daily impact she had on our students and staff. Her legacy remains a guiding light for our district. At this time, please join me in a moment of silence to honor the life of Mrs. Boyd.

Carol Hermsen dedicated her career to serving students and families through school transportation, beginning with the city of Newport News before continuing with Chesterfield County Public Schools. From 1991 until her retirement in 2011, she proudly served as a special needs school bus driver.

Her last assigned bus was bus 225, where her patience, kindness, and compassion touched the lives of countless students and families. Carol had a special passion for Special Olympics and found great joy in supporting the athletes and celebrating their achievements.

Her legacy of service, compassion, and dedication will be remembered by all who had the privilege of knowing and working with her. Please join me in a moment of silence for those we have lost. Heavenly Father, we come to you this evening as we are excited to start a new school year in just a few weeks.

Father, we thank you for those who have gone before us and have paid the way of excellence in their work. The students that have gone before us, Father, that have left lasting impact. We lift them up to you and we pray for their families. Father, as we focus on the 26th, 27th school year, we ask that you go before us, that you would be with this board in the decisions that it makes, that we would work collaboratively and effectively and efficiently for our community, for our teachers, for our staff.

Lord, that you're with our bus drivers in the over 9 million miles that they will drive this year, that you're with our cafeteria workers as they provide the nutrition that is very much needed to sustain our kids during the school day. We pray for our teachers who pour themselves into the daily educating of our students.

We thank you for the administration and staff in front office. We thank you for our custodians who work diligently to clean our schools and to ensure that our children and our teachers come to a school that is clean and presentable and sets the expectation for the high education.

Father, thank you for the opportunity to be in Chesterfield County. Thank you for the opportunity to send our kids to school. Lord, we ask that you're with us and in this meeting, and we ask all of these things. In your Son, Jesus' name I pray. Amen.

Please join us at this time in the Pledge of Allegiance. The flag of the United States of America, thanks to the republic for which it stands, one nation, under God, indivisible, with liberty and justice for all.

Two teams from Cheshire County Public Schools made a lot of money in the stock market game. In the annual game organized by Virginia Council on Economic Education, student teams compete for awards by investing $100,000 in a virtual portfolio across 10 weeks.

John Randall coaches the team at Silver Creek Middle. Team members earn a 23.6% profit, placing first in Virginia for middle school teams this spring. Their portfolio is valued at close to $130,000. Paul Klein coaches the team at Manchester High. Team members earned a 39.8% profit, beating out more than 1,000 teams across Virginia.
